subject: Dedicated GPU capacity: planning deep-dive request
messages:
From: Jill Park <jill.park@orion-analytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orion-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU capacity: initial planning request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the Orion platform team is keen to run an architecture-level deep-dive on dedicated GPU capacity before we commit to a Reserved capacity plan. Main items we want to cover: pool sizing to match peak inference qps, autoscaling behavior during batch vs. streaming workloads, and isolation/networking options for regulatory boundaries.

Can your team do a 60–90 minute technical session in the next two weeks? Preferably with someone from infra/serving runtime and an SRE/ops contact who can talk failover and maintenance windows.

Background: we plan to serve a mix of 2.5–6k concurrent API clients, peak 450 tokens/sec aggregated, model mix includes a 13B decoder and a quantized 70B for batch reporting. We will need some separation between customer workloads (logical isolation), and strong audit logs for compliance.

Proposed times that work for us: Dec 11 13:00–14:30 PST, Dec 14 10:00–11:30 PST, or week of Dec 21 if needed.

Appreciate any suggested agenda and pre-reads.

Regards,
Jill Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Orion Analytics

Hi Jill — thanks for the clear requirements. We can absolutely run a focused architecture review.

High-level availability: Dec 16 14:00–15:30 PST (we have a few internal constraints earlier in the week). If that works, we’ll make it a 75-minute session: 15 min context + 45 min deep technical walkthrough + 15 min Q&A and next steps.

Draft agenda (attached):
- Intro & success criteria (Marissa)
- Workload signals & modeling (Aisha)
- Pool sizing heuristics and capacity calculator (Karthik)
- Autoscaling strategies: latency vs cost tradeoffs (Neha)
- Isolation patterns: tenant isolation, VPC, and auditability (Neha)
- Ops runbook & failover (Marissa)

Can you confirm:
1) target 95th p50/p99 latency SLOs for API calls?
2) expected steady-state vs burst ratio (e.g., 70/30 steady/burst)?
3) any hard constraints on on-prem vs cloud-only?

Attaching a short draft agenda for your review. I’ll also share a capacity calculator and a simple topology sketch in the next message.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick update: Dec 14 we have a client-facing blackout and Dec 16 is still our preferred window but we need the session to finish by 15:30 PST due to an internal executive sync. Can you also send any SOC 2 and network isolation docs ahead of the meeting? Procurement will need those for vendor review.

Regarding your clarifying questions:
- 70B will be quantized to int8 for now (may look at int4 later).
- We prefer strictly dedicated GPUs for the reporting workload; preemptible is okay for non-critical batch jobs.
- Logging/audit sinks need to be in an audited S3 bucket; peering is acceptable if we can lock down flow logs and have read-only credentials for the bucket.

If Dec 16 14:00–15:30 PST works on your side, please send calendar invite and pre-reads.

Best,
Jill

Hi Jill — confirmed for Dec 16, 14:00–15:30 PST. Calendar invite: https://calendar.redwood.ai/invite/ORION-2026-09-DEC16 (you should have received this).

Attachments included for pre-read: capacity_calculator_v2.xlsx, gpu_topology_sketch.png. Marissa will cover runbook/maintenance windows and I’ll walk through pool-sizing heuristics and tradeoffs. Neha (cc’d) will take autoscaling and isolation sections.

Quick notes we’ll cover and want you to confirm live:
- Sizing: planner assumes int8 70B = 42 GB GPU working set; we’ll show math for mixed model pools and hot vs cold routing.
- Autoscale: continuous batching thresholds, token-per-second triggers, and a fast-path for low-latency streaming.
- Isolation: tenant-level cgroups + virtualized KV cache partitioning, VPC segmentation patterns and audit sinks.
- Ops: maintenance window best practices and how we hold steady-state during rolling upgrades.

If you have a short list of utterly-blocking questions (e.g., hard latency <80ms at p95), point them here and we’ll prioritize those slides.

See you tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik
